title: Due Diligence One-Pager: SOC2 / ISO / HIPAA Comparison and Sales-ready Evidence
content:
Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Redwood must present a concise, defensible one‑pager that helps Sales and CSE get through technical due diligence quickly for SOC2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA-focused prospects. This doc is a working one-pager + evidence checklist + suggested customer-facing language for RFPs and rapid security calls. It assumes the audience already knows basic LLM concepts and focuses on what customers ask about most: audit logs, data flows, retention, encryption/KMS, and BAAs.

Purpose and use cases (how to use this doc):
- Quick handout for CSE to paste into an initial security email.
- Appendix to RFP responses (short version).
- Talking points for AE/CISO-briefing calls.
- Checklist for Solutions Eng when assembling technical evidence.

Core positioning statement (1–2 lines):
Redwood provides production‑grade inference with enterprise controls: immutable, per‑request audit logging; customer‑controlled key management; region‑aware data controls; and a private deployment model that satisfies HIPAA and ISO/SOC due diligence with documented evidence packages.

What buyers actually ask (top themes observed in last 12 months):
- Can you demonstrate immutable audit trails and the level of detail (input, model, output, timestamp, actor)?
- How do you segregate customer data between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments?
- What encryption/KMS options are available (BYOK/HSM)?
- Can you sign a BAA and what parts of the platform are covered?
- How long do you retain logs and how can the customer control retention?
- How do you support eDiscovery/forensics requests?
- Which ISO 27001 controls and SOC2 TSC trust services are you mapping to?

Suggested one‑paragraph proof point for sales emails (copy/paste):
We provide per‑request audit logs (request id, user id, model + version, request metadata, token counts, response hash) retained under customer-configurable policies, optional automatic redaction, and support for BYOK/HSM so keys remain under customer control. For regulated workloads we offer Private deployments (VPC or on‑prem) with BAA support and ISO/SOC evidence packages — happy to share our readiness checklist and recent SOC2 report under NDA.

Evidence checklist (what Solutions Eng should bundle for an enterprise lead):
- SOC2 Type II report (most recent) — redacted if required
- ISO 27001 scope statement and certificate (if available)
- Signed BAA template with list of covered services and delegation of responsibilities
- Audit log sample (anonymized) showing request id, timestamps, model/version, request/response sizes, and authorized principal
- Architecture diagram showing network boundaries (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and where logs are stored
- KMS architecture and proof of BYOK/HSM integration (diagrams, procedure docs)
- Data retention and deletion policy text excerpts (how to configure retention per-customer)
- EDR/forensics runbook and incident response timeline template
- Pen test summary and remediation notes (last 12 months)
- Privacy & DLP controls overview (PII redaction options, regex hooks, pre-send transforms)

Mapping to compliance frameworks (short):
- SOC2 (TSC): Audit logging, availability, confidentiality, and change-management evidence map to our runtime and control plane. Prepare: logging config screenshots, access control lists, RBAC roles, and alerting/tracing examples.
- ISO 27001: Map typical clauses: A.8 (asset mgmt) for model artifacts; A.9 (access control) for IAM/KMS; A.12 (operation security) for runtime hardening and patching; A.16 (info security incident mgmt) for incident response. Provide: scope statement and control mappings.
- HIPAA: Provide BAA commitment + technical controls: encryption at rest/in transit, access logs, role-based access, private deployment option. Clarify: hosted API customers should not send PHI unless contractually agreed and BAA signed; recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated reserved capacity for PHI.

Audit log language (short templates to include in proposals) — two variants: technical and executive
- Executive: "We retain an immutable audit trail for each inference request (identifier, principal, model version, input/response metadata). Audit logs can be retained per-customer with configurable retention policies and are available for export to customer SIEMs."
- Technical: "Audit record schema: request_id, timestamp_utc, principal_id, principal_type, model_name, model_version, prompt_hash (sha256), prompt_token_count, response_token_count, response_hash (sha256), route, region, inference_latency_ms, storage_location_uri. Logs are write-once, append-only, and signed with a service-level key; exports can be configured to push to customer S3 / Azure Blob with server-side encryption using customer-managed keys (BYOK)."

Retention & immutability guidance (recommended default language):
- Default hosted retention: 90 days for request bodies, 365 days for metadata (configurable).
- Dedicated/Private: retention fully customer-configurable; for HIPAA we recommend retention consistent with customer policy and include delete-on-demand support via API and ticketed forenscis export.
- Immutability: logs are stored append-only with periodic digest signing; for deep compliance customers offer signed ledger export (monthly digests) to customer storage.

Sample BAA clause (short):
-"Provider will implement administrative, physical and technical safeguards to protect PHI as required by HIPAA. Provider will enter into a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) covering the services outlined in the scope. Provider will provide audit logs and evidence of access to PHI on request as part of incident response and eDiscovery needs."

Competitive positioning notes (what to highlight vs each competitor type):
- Public cloud AI endpoints (major clouds): call out that Redwood provides uniform controls across hosted/dedicated/private with clear evidence packages; emphasize predictable latency SLAs, signing keys, and model variant fallbacks that clouds do not bundle with a single contract. Highlight: audit log schema and digest signing, private deployment option with BAA, and per-route cost/latency dashboards.
- LLM API incumbents (simple API players): stress enterprise-grade observability and auditability (per-request attribution, KV/prefix cache controls), and advanced operational controls (canary rollouts, auto-fallback rules) not typical of lightweight APIs.
- Self-hosted inference stacks / open-source ops: emphasize Redwood’s hardened runtime, kernel/quantization testing evidence, and managed processes for patching/pen tests and compliance reporting. Note: self-hosted can give full control but higher ops burden — position Redwood as lower-risk, faster time-to-compliance.

Top objections & suggested rebuttals (concise):
- Objection: "We need a BAA and PHI processing—can you sign?"
  Rebuttal: "Yes. We support BAAs. For PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated deployment; for hosted usage we can review case-by-case and lock contract terms. I'll loop in legal and solutions eng and share our standard BAA template under NDA."
- Objection: "Your audit logs don’t capture full prompts (we can’t send PHI anyway)."
  Rebuttal: "Logs capture hashes and metadata by default; for customers needing full bodies for forensics we offer configurable retention (with appropriate contractual safeguards) and direct export to customer-controlled storage."
- Objection: "We require BYOK/HSM with key separation."
  Rebuttal: "We support BYOK integration and HSM-backed keys for both hosting and Private deployments; we can provide our key lifecycle and rotation docs and an architecture diagram for review."

Technical appendix (short bullets Solutions Eng often needs):
- Where logs are written: regional object storage + archival copies in a secondary region (configurable).
- Who can access logs: RBAC with audit trail; support for SCIM provisioning and Okta SSO; logs access gated with approval workflows.
- Export paths: S3/Azure Blob/GCS sink; SIEM connectors (Splunk, Datadog) via secure push or pull with signed URLs.
- Hashing approach: prompt/response are SHA‑256 hashed in transit to logs if retention of raw text is disabled.
- Redaction options: configurable regex or ML-based PII scrubbing pre-write (deployable at edge for Private customers).
- Digest signing: monthly Merkle/digest file produced and optionally pushed to customer storage for immutable proof.

Competitive intel notes (what we've seen in RFPs lately):
- Customers want examples of "audit search queries" (we should produce quick sample Kibana/Splunk search terms).
- Requests for "token-level billing reconciliation" are increasing — include token counts in audit logs.
- Growing interest in "forensic snapshots" (full request+response exports for a date range) — we need a standardized ticketed workflow and SLA.

Sales playbook snippets (one-liners and next steps):
- Email opener: "Happy to share our SOC2 report + short evidence pack. Would you like the redacted SOC2 or the full under NDA? Also, do you prefer a BAA discussion now or when we reach commercial terms?"
- Call play: "We typically cover (1) where your PHI lives, (2) which deployment model you want (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and (3) retention/forensics requirements — that determines the evidence we provide."
- Next step checklist to propose to a prospect: NDA -> Share redacted SOC2 -> BAA negotiation (if PHI) -> Solutions Eng evidence bundle -> Security deep-dive.

Open items / follow ups (internal):
- Create sample Kibana/Splunk search queries and add to evidence pack (owner: Diego).
- Finalize digest-signing architecture diagram and wording for sales (owner: Jordan).
- Update hosted default retention values in product docs to match the wording above (owner: Product Docs).
- Package a "forensics export playbook" for CSE with ticket templates and SLA commitments.

Quick references and links (internal references):
- Internal SOC2 FAQ page: confluence:sec/soc2-faq-2025
- BAA template (draft): google-drive:legal/baa-templates/baa-redwood-2025.docx
- Audit schema spec (dev): github:repo/audit-schema/README.md

Tone guidance for CSE/AEs (dos & don’ts):
- DO: Use the executive proof point and offer to share SOC2 under NDA.
- DO: Ask early whether prospect will send PHI and recommend Private/Dedicated early if yes.
- DON’T: Promise specific retention periods for hosted customers without validating the current product defaults.
- DON’T: Overload the first email with attachments — offer the redacted report and wait for an NDA for full artifacts.

Appendix: sample short FAQ to paste into proposals (3 Qs)
Q: Can we get a copy of your SOC2?
A: Yes — we can share a redacted SOC2 Type II immediately and the full one under NDA.
Q: Do you sign BAAs?
A: Yes — we offer a standard BAA and can negotiate where required. For PHI we recommend Private/Dedicated.
Q: How do you handle customer key management?
A: We support BYOK with HSM-backed CMKs; we can provide key lifecycle docs and architecture diagrams.

End notes (status & next review):
This is a working one-pager intended for CSE and AE use; please add edits inline. Plan to iterate monthly as product retention defaults and evidence packages change. Next review scheduled 2026-03-15.
